speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You presented with sudden onset abdominal pain; to begin our evaluation, could you please describe the exact location of the pain and how severe it is on a scale of one to ten?

speaker: Patient
text: 74-year-old male. The patient presents with sudden onset of abdominal pain around the umbilicus 16 hours ago, with recent history of hospitalization for an acute myocardial infarction a week ago. Reports several episodes of bloody loose bowel movements. Denies vomiting.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Ischemic Colitis. Given the patient's recent myocardial infarction and sudden onset of bloody diarrhea with periumbilical pain, this presentation is highly suggestive of ischemic colitis caused by low-flow states or embolic events. I recommend immediate evaluation with an urgent colonoscopy to confirm the diagnosis and assess bowel viability.
